children: , the electric-vehicle and AI-robotics company, entered a closely watched California discrimination trial Monday tied to allegations involving its Fremont factory. Shares gained approximately 3% to $375.17, showing investors were looking past the immediate legal headline as trading remained firmly positive.

California alleges Black workers faced harassment, unequal pay and fewer opportunities for promotion at the plant. Tesla denies wrongdoing, says discrimination is prohibited under its policies and has said employees responsible for misconduct have been dismissed. Judge Peter Borkon has scheduled the bench trial to run through October 30, meaning the legal issue could remain in the background for Tesla investors for several weeks.

The valuation picture adds another layer. Tesla's $375.17 share price sits 12.33% above its GF Value estimate of $333.99, showing the market is already assigning the company a meaningful premium over GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. California law does not impose a cap on potential damages, but neither liability nor any financial award has been determined. For shareholders, the bigger question is whether the proceedings ultimately remain a contained legal expense or expose broader weaknesses in workplace oversight, employee retention and operating controls at one of Tesla's most important manufacturing sites.

title: Tesla Gains 3% as Fremont Bias Claims Reach Trial
